message.content:
Here’s a quick roundup of well‑received documentaries you can watch (or stream) if you’re interested in learning more about climate change:

| Title | Release year | Platform(s) | Why It Stands Out |
|-------|--------------|-------------|-------------------|
| **“An Inconvenient Truth”** | 2006 | Netflix, Amazon Prime Video, YouTube Movies | Former Vice President Al Gore presents science & policy arguments in an accessible way—great for beginners. |
| **“Before the Flood”** | 2017 | Disney+, Hulu, Amazon Prime Video | Leonardo DiCaprio travels worldwide, meeting scientists, activists, and leaders while highlighting human impact. |
| **“Our Planet – Climate Change Special”** | 2020 | BBC Earth / Discovery+ | A visually stunning nature series paired with a dedicated episode on how ecosystems are shifting due to warming. |
| **“Climate Refugee”** | 2018 | PBS, Apple TV+ | Focuses on people displaced by rising seas and extreme weather events, giving a personal perspective on adaptation challenges. |
| **“Heat Death of the World”** | 2021 | National Geographic, HBO Max | Explores future scenarios from a physics standpoint, including runaway greenhouse effects and planetary limits. |
| **“A Plastic Ocean”** | 2019 | Netflix, Amazon Prime Video | While primarily about plastic pollution, it ties oceanic changes directly to temperature rise and marine life loss. |
| **“Ice Fall”** | 2022 | CuriosityStream, Amazon Prime Video | Examines melting ice sheets through time-lapse footage, showing real-time evidence of glacial retreat. |

### How to Get Started
* Pick one that matches your preferred format (talk‑show style vs. field‑reporter).
* Many streaming services offer free trials—use them to sample before committing.
* For deeper dives after watching, look up related academic papers or follow organizations like IPCC, NASA GISS, or NOAA.

Enjoy exploring this critical issue!
